title: Machine-learning protein classifier separates follicular thyroid adenoma from carcinoma
summary: From 2443 samples of 1568 patients across 24 centres, machine-learning models on DNA and protein features were compared, and the discovery protein model (AUC 0.899) outperformed the gene-based model (AUC 0.670). A 24-protein targeted mass-spectrometry model reached AUCs of 0.871 and 0.853 in two retrospective sets and 0.781 in prospective fine-needle aspirations, with a negative predictive value of 95.7% for ruling out malignant nodules. Preprint; the prospective AUC is modest.
ai_technology: Machine-learning classifiers on DNA and protein features, with a 24-protein targeted model
organization: Westlake University; Affiliated Hangzhou First People's Hospital, Westlake University, School of Medicine

evidence.tested: Validation in three independent testing sets, two retrospective and one prospective fine-needle aspiration cohort.
evidence.unknown: Clinical utility and whether the prospective set used a frozen model; full text not reviewed.
